title: Hosting sensitivity and KPI intake - Orrin Analytics
summary: Initial economics and hosting intake focused on how batching, KV/prefix caching and hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) affect per-token cost and latency under Orrin's multitenant conversational workload. Customer has a $120k Q4 inference budget target, strong P95 latency SLA (<=250ms token), and needs SOC2 + KMS. Discussed pilot scope, benchmarks, and next steps to size Dedicated pool and run an on-prem smoke test.
action_items: Marco Diaz: Share sample benchmark config + perf spreadsheet (due: 2025-08-07)
Aisha Patel: Send high-level pricing sheet for hosted and 3 dedicated tiers (due: 2025-08-05)
Priya Menon / Marco: Schedule pilot capacity test (30m) - target week of 2025-08-18
Jules Nguyen: Provide SOC2 + KMS integration doc link (due: 2025-08-06)
next_steps: AE to email pricing and contract options
SE to run token-level throughput sensitivity test with customer prompts
Schedule 30m pilot benchmark with dev/test dataset
Customer to confirm peak qps and token distribution by 2025-08-08
transcript:
Meeting: 2025-08-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Recording link: https://redwood.app/meetings/ff-20250803-orrin-001 (redacted)
Shared: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/hosted-vs-dedicated.pdf, perf sheet link sent after

[00:00] Aisha Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Aisha with Redwood, AE. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Sophie Lane: Sophie here, head of ML at Orrin.
[00:10] David Cho: David, CTO.
[00:12] Priya Menon: Priya, infra.
[00:14] Noah Brooks: Noah, product.
[00:16] Marco Diaz: Marco, solutions engineer at Redwood.
[00:19] Jules Nguyen: Jules from CS.

[00:30] Aisha: Cool, goal for today is to understand your cost constraints and latency SLOs so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private and outline a pilot. Sophie, can you give us a quick description of the workload?
[00:45] Sophie: Yeah, so we've got a consumer-facing chat assistant, about 300k monthly active users but only ~10% daily, so for inference it's spiky. Typical session has multiple turns, avg tokens per request is around 220 but with a long-tail where some requests hit 800 tokens, and we also do reranking for search which is short, like 40 tokens. 
[01:15] Sophie: Latency is important, product team wants p95 per-token latency below 250 milliseconds for chat to keep UX snappy.

[01:30] Aisha: OK. And budget?
[01:32] David: We have about $120k for inference run in Q4 as a cap, ideally less but that's our runway target.
[01:40] Marco: Understood. So tradeoffs we'll discuss: batch size windows, prefix/KV cache to reduce token generation, quantization options if you go private/dedicated, and routing policies for burst capacity.

[02:00] Priya: For security, SOC2 is required and we need KMS for key management if any customer PII is in logs. Also prefer VPC peering if we go private.
[02:12] Jules: We have SOC2 docs we can share.

[02:30] Marco: Great. Quick question on traffic shape — what's your peak RPS and typical concurrent users?
[02:36] Noah: Peak 80 qps during promo spikes, normally 6-8 qps, session length varies.

[03:00] Marco: Ok that's helpful. On-hosted, our per-token model pricing includes streaming and has predictable CPU/GPU tick; Dedicated lets you reserve GPU pool which reduces per-token unit cost but you pay for reserved capacity. Private adds ops overhead but lets you use quantized models (4-bit) and on-prem infra which can further lower cost.

[03:30] Sophie: Can you walk through an example? If we do 220 tokens average and say 50 qps sustained during peak, what does hosted vs dedicated look like?
[03:42] Marco: Sure, quick ballpark — hosted per-token (unoptimized) might be $0.0009 per token at the high end for large-context models; with batching and caching that effective can drop to $0.00035 - $0.0006 depending on hit-rate. Dedicated reserved pool can get to $0.0002 - $0.0004 per effective token if you achieve high utilization and use preemptible pricing for some capacity. These are rough numbers, we'll send a detailed sheet.
[04:15] David: That hosted per-token number seems high for our budget; we need to see the unit economics for our token distribution.
[04:25] Aisha: Totally. We'll run the perf spreadsheet with your token histogram.

[04:40] Marco: Important lever is KV/prefix caching — if you cache the system prompt and first 256 tokens of common flows you can avoid recomputing those tokens on each request which drops generated tokens.
[04:55] Sophie: How does that affect latency? Is caching adding network hop?
[05:00] Marco: There's a small lookup cost but it's usually <10ms, far outweighed by the saved decode time for cached tokens. Also batching windows — if you increase the batching window from 10ms to 50ms you can increase batch size and lower per-token GPU time, but that adds tail latency.

[05:25] Priya: For us p95 must remain <=250ms, so long batching windows might break SLA.
[05:32] Marco: Right, so you tune batching per route — low-latency chat route with small window, background rerank route with larger window. Redwood supports per-route policies.

[06:00] Sophie: Any fallback options if dedicated pool gets saturated?
[06:04] Marco: We have smart routing and automatic fallback to hosted region or cheaper model variant — you can set policies which prefer dedicated but fall back to hosted with a compatible model. That affects cost but keeps service up.

[06:25] Noah: For budgeting — do you expose token breakdown by route in the console?
[06:30] Jules: Yes, per-route cost and token level breakdowns, and token categorization (system, prompt, completion).

[06:45] David: Can you quantify the impact of 4-bit quantization? It sounds attractive but worried about quality regression on our reranker.
[06:55] Marco: 4-bit quant often yields 1.1-1.3x slower decode on some kernels but halves memory. For many decoder-only models quality is preserved, but for reranking you should run evals — we can recommend models validated by Redwood. We also provide automatic rollbacks if quality drifts.

[07:25] Sophie: So immediate next steps: we need pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated reserved monthly tiers vs private on-prem), and a bench run using our sample prompt set.

[07:35] Aisha: We'll do that. Marco, can you outline the pilot technical scope?
[07:40] Marco: Pilot scope: 1) run the perf tests with sample prompts to produce per-token latency and throughput for the model you choose; 2) test prefix/KV cache hit rates with synthetic session traces; 3) run a short dedicated pool soak with your concurrency shape; 4) measure cost under different batching windows. We'll aim for a 2-week pilot if you want deeper soak, but initial 48h benchmark gives good signals.

[08:12] Priya: For the pilot, could it be in our VPC or do you prefer hosted? We need to validate KMS + VPC peering.
[08:18] Marco: We can do both — a hosted pilot with VPC peering to test network + KMS, or a private deployment for the full on-prem test. Hosted with VPC peering is faster to stand up.

[08:40] Sophie: Does Redwood charge setup for private?
[08:44] Aisha: Private has a platform fee + deployment fee; Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract monthly. We'll include those in the pricing doc.

[09:00] Noah: About burst capacity — can we burst beyond reserved GPUs to handle promos?
[09:05] Marco: Yes, Dedicated has configured autoscale and burst to hosted. You can define burst limits and cost controls to allow short-term oversubscription.

[09:20] David: We're worried about a worst-case cost during a spike — is there a way to cap spend per minute or per day?
[09:27] Jules: Console supports per-route budgets and alerts. Also token throttles and circuit-breakers to force fallbacks when spend thresholds hit.

[09:40] Sophie: Hypothetical: a 10x traffic surge for 2 hours — what happens?
[09:45] Marco: If you allow bursting, you'll pay for hosted fallbacks; if you want hard caps, you can set throttles so requests get queue or degrade. For user-facing chat we'd usually recommend soft fallback to a smaller model with graceful degradation.

[10:10] Priya: Are logs and audit traces kept separate per customer on Dedicated?
[10:14] Marco: Yes, Dedicated offers tenant isolation; Private means you control the logs entirely. Hosted keeps logs in our tenancy but you can opt out of storing completions.

[10:30] David: For encryption, how is KMS integrated?
[10:34] Jules: KMS via customer-managed keys can be set up for private and dedicated, and hosted supports bring-your-own-key for certain tiers. We'll send the integration doc.

[10:50] Sophie: About perf numbers again — can we see an example spreadsheet with sensitivity to batching window and hit rate?
[10:57] Marco: We'll send that — for example a 50% cache hit can reduce generated tokens by ~40% depending on overlap; combine with batching you can see >60% unit cost reduction for chat-heavy workloads.

[11:20] David: Sounds promising, but we need a clear recommendation for Q4: stay hosted + caching + throttles, or move to Dedicated reserved pool?
[11:28] Aisha: Quick rule of thumb — if your steady-state sustained qps during business hours justifies the reserved cost (we'll run numbers), Dedicated wins on unit economics; if traffic is highly spiky and budget tight, start hosted with caching and move to Dedicated as usage solidifies.

[11:48] Sophie: What's the commitment length for Dedicated discounts?
[11:52] Aisha: Typical reserved terms are 6 or 12 months with increasing discounts. We'll show both.

[12:05] Noah: Any risks to model compatibility when we switch between hosted and private?
[12:10] Marco: Models are abstracted — we provide compatible variants; sometimes you need a quantized build for private which can slightly change behavior; we recommend running evals and the rollout can be managed via Redwood's canary/rollback tooling.

[12:35] Priya: For our Security team, they'll want SOC2 docs and also a whitepaper on network topology for VPC peering.
[12:42] Jules: We'll send SOC2 and topography.

[13:00] Marco: Quick deep dive — batching. We typically use dynamic batching with a max window per route. For chat route we use 8-12ms windows by default, for rerank 30-60ms. That keeps p95 low for chat.

[13:25] Sophie: 8-12ms seems tiny, how do you get benefits?
[13:28] Marco: Even small windows can group a few concurrent requests, especially in spikes; combined with continuous batching across workers it helps. But yes, long-tail requests still determine p95.

[13:50] David: Are there extra savings from fragment caching (partial KV reuse)?
[13:55] Marco: Yes, partial KV reuse where you reuse cached K/V for prefixes can save compute on initial layers; for models with big context windows this is material. We'll model it in the perf sheet.

[14:20] Sophie: Let's talk timeline — if we want to pilot before end of August, what's realistic?
[14:24] Aisha: If you send token histograms and sample prompts by Aug 8, we can run a bench and get results by Aug 14 and propose a pilot for Aug 18.

[14:40] Noah: We'll aim to send the data. Any blockers on your side for a hosted pilot?
[14:45] Marco: No blockers — hosted pilot with VPC peering and KMS needs network details and IAM roles. For Dedicated pilot we'll need expected concurrency to size the pool.

[15:05] Sophie: One operational question — who owns model updates? We want predictable rollouts.
[15:10] Marco: You can pin model versions per route; Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback if quality drops.

[15:28] David: On cost modeling, do you support a blended view combining hosted and reserved usage?
[15:33] Jules: Yes, console shows blended billing and per-route forecasts so you can see how routing policies affect spend.

[15:50] Aisha: Quick calibration, Sophie — based on your numbers what is your acceptable monthly spend target?
[15:57] Sophie: We want to keep Q4 below $120k. Monthly that's ~40k. If we run pilot and see dedicated reduces unit cost enough, we can justify reserving.

[16:12] Marco: We'll run scenarios at 10k, 30k, 50k monthly token volumes and show tipping points for dedicated.

[16:30] (brief pause/crosstalk)

[17:00] Sophie: Could you also include the quality/regression guardrails — e.g. eval thresholds that would trigger a rollback?
[17:06] Marco: Yes we can propose evaluation thresholds (perplexity/ROUGE or custom metrics using your test set) and wire those into automatic rollouts.

[17:30] David: For the pilot, would we need an NDA?
[17:33] Aisha: We already have a mutual NDA on file but we'll check and send confirmation.

[17:45] Noah: Any specific prompts that typically show the most sensitivity to quantization?
[17:50] Marco: Reranking and code-gen styles are more sensitive. We'll request a few sample prompts that exercise those cases.

[18:10] Priya: About logs retention — we need 90-day retention with audit logs for compliance. Is that supported?
[18:15] Jules: Yes, retention windows are configurable for Dedicated and Private; hosted has tiers. We'll include retention pricing.

[18:35] Sophie: Ok can we recap action items?
[18:38] Aisha: Sure — Marco bench config + perf sheet, Aisha pricing sheet, Jules SOC2/KMS docs, schedule pilot.

[18:50] Marco: I'll also include a sample rollback policy snippet and an example of per-route batching config.

[19:10] David: One last question — do you have any live customers in our space (analytics + consumer chat)?
[19:16] Aisha: Yes, we have a couple references in fintech and retail with similar patterns; we'll provide anonymized case studies.

[19:30] Sophie: Great.

[19:40] Aisha: If there are no further questions we'll wrap.
[19:44] Priya: No further from infra.
[19:46] David: Nothing else.
[19:48] Noah: All set.

[19:55] Aisha: Thanks everyone — expect the pricing + perf sheet by Aug 5 and the benchmark config. We'll reconnect after you send the token histograms.
[20:05] Sophie: Thanks all.

[20:10] (call ends, notes: approximate timestamps; transcription has small errors e.g., 'Redwood Dedicate' sometimes clipped)

Notes: transcript contains a few auto-caption misrecognitions especially for product names, proper nouns.
